designationHistory.indexText: The Fish and Wildlife Service established Valle de Oro National Wildlife Refuge in Albuquerque on September 21, 2012, with the purchase of about 390 acres of a former dairy farm, the first urban wildlife refuge in the Southwest.

authority.citation: Land acquisition by the Fish and Wildlife Service (establishment notice 78 FR 35640)

designationHistory.note: Pass A (Federal Register notice: established September 21, 2012, with a purchase of 389 acres) and Pass B (Interior press release of September 27, 2012: formally established "last Friday," i.e. September 21, through acquisition of 390 acres; dedicated September 27) agree. The fws.gov About page says it was dedicated August 8, 2012, which conflicts with both and is not used.

sources.name: Federal Register, Establishment of the Valle de Oro National Wildlife Refuge, 78 FR 35640 (June 13, 2013)
U.S. Department of the Interior press release, "Salazar Dedicates Two National Wildlife Refuges in New Mexico" (Sept. 27, 2012)
